parts.problem_md:
In a group of 200 students:

- 120 study Chemistry $( C )$,
- 90 study Geography $(G)$,
- 50 study both Chemistry and Geography.

Draw a Venn diagram to represent this information.
parts.solution_md:
> *Draw a Venn diagram with two labelled circles and fill in 50 in the overlapping region*

![Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labelled C and G. The overlap contains the number 50](assets/001-venn-diagram-with-two-overlapping-circles-labell.png)

**[B1]**

> *120 study Chemistry in total*

*120 - 50 = 70*

![Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labelled C and G. The overlap contains the number 50, the C only section contains 70](assets/002-venn-diagram-with-two-overlapping-circles-labell.png)

**[B1]**

> *90 study Geography in total*

*90 - 50 = 40*

![Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labelled C and G. The overlap contains the number 50, the C only section contains 70, G only section contains 40](assets/003-venn-diagram-with-two-overlapping-circles-labell.png)

**[B1]**

> *Calculate how many students from the 200 study neither Chemistry nor Geography*

*200 - 70 - 50 - 40 = 40*

![Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labelled C and G. The overlap contains the number 50, the C only section contains 70, G only section contains 40, outside section contains 40](assets/004-venn-diagram-with-two-overlapping-circles-labell.png)

**[B1]**

parts.problem_md:
A student is selected at random.

Find:

(i) $P ( C \cup G )$.

(ii) $P ( ( C \cup G ) ' )$.

(iii) $P ( ( C \cap G ) ' )$.
parts.solution_md:
![Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labelled C and G. The overlap contains the number 50, the C only section contains 70, G only section contains 40, outside section contains 40](assets/004-venn-diagram-with-two-overlapping-circles-labell.png)

(i)

> $P ( C \cup G )$* means the probability that the selected student studies Chemistry or Geography*

$\frac{70+50+40}{200}=\frac{160}{200}$

$P ( C \cup G ) = \frac{4}{5}$

**[B1]**

(ii)

> $P ( ( C \cup G ) ' )$* means the probability of not studying "Chemistry OR Geography"*

> *i.e. It means *$1 - P ( C \cup G )$

> *These are the students not in either circle*

> *It is also equal to 1 minus the answer to part (i)*

$\frac{40}{200}$

$P ( ( C \cup G ) ' ) = 1 \frac{1}{5}$

**[B1]**

(iii)

> $P ( ( C \cap G ) ' )$* means the probability of not studying "Chemistry AND Geography"*

> *This is any student not in the overlapping region*

$\frac{70+40+40}{200}=\frac{150}{200}$

$P ( ( C \cap G ) ' ) = \frac{3}{4}$

**[B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Exact equivalent answers are also accepted for each mark.
> 
> E.g. $\frac{150}{200}$ instead of $\frac{3}{4}$.

parts.problem_md:
The Venn diagram shows information about the number of students in a class who like apples ($A$) and bananas ($B$).

![qp5a-0580-33-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/005-qp5a-0580-33-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

One of the students is chosen at random.

Find the probability that this student does not like apples and does not like bananas.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> *Add together all of the numbers in the Venn diagram to work out how many students there are in total*

*12 + 8 + 7 + 4 = 31 *

> *Express the number of students who liked neither apples or bananas, 4 (outside the circles), as a fraction of the total number of students, 31*

$\frac{4}{31}$ **[1]**

A child is chosen at random from the children who have a computer.   
Write down the probability that this child also has a phone.
parts.solution_md:
*As we are choosing a child from those who have a computer, we are only considering those within the highlighted "have a computer" circle* *Out of these, we are looking for children who also have a phone, this is in the overlapping section*

> *The probability is therefore*

$\frac{8}{8+7}=\frac{8}{15}$

$\frac{8}{15}$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
At a fitness centre, the number of members using the exercise machines (*E*), the swimming pool (*S*) and the tennis courts (*T*) is shown on the Venn diagram.

![cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-1-p4-q10c](assets/012-cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-1-p4-q10c.png)

A member using the swimming pool is chosen at random. Find the probability that this member also uses the tennis courts and the exercise machines.
parts.solution_md:
*The probability of an event occurring = *$\frac{\mathrm{number} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{ways} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{event} \mathrm{can} \mathrm{occur}}{\mathrm{total} \mathrm{number} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{possible} \mathrm{outcomes}}$ *We know from Q10(c)(ii) that 50 people use the swimming pool. *
*So the denominator is 50* *Of those people, 4 people use the exercise machines and the tennis court. *
*So the numerator is 4*

**Identifying denominator as 50, or numerator as 4****  [1]**

$\frac{4}{50}\mathrm{or}\frac{2}{25}$**[1]**

The Venn diagram shows information about the number of elements in sets A, B and calligraphic E.

An element is chosen at random from $E$. 
Find the probability that this element is in $(A\cupB)'$.
parts.solution_md:
> $(A\cupB)'$* means the compliment of *$(A\cupB)$*, or everything that's not in *$A$*or *$B$*. *
*It is the unshaded region in the diagram below.*

![n9Cij2p7_cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-tz2-p2-q23](assets/022-n9cij2p7-cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-tz2-p2-q23.png)

*Total number of items = 7 + 23 = 30*

$P(A\cupB)'=\frac{7}{30}$

**numerator is 7**** [1] **
**denominator is 30**** [1]**

parts.problem_md:
There are 32 students in a class.

5 do not study any languages. 15 study German (G). 18 study Spanish (S).

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9a](assets/026-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9a.png)

Complete the Venn diagram to show this information.
parts.solution_md:
> *5 do not study any languages, so place 5 in the Venn diagram outside of both bubbles.*

> *Find the intersection of both bubbles *$( G \cap S )$* by finding how many students have been counted twice in German and Spanish.*

> * *

*German + Spanish - both + neither = 32 *

*15 + 18 - both + 5 = 32 *

*38 - both = 32*

*both = 6*

**[1]**

** **

> *Place 6 in the Venn diagram in the intersection of both bubbles.*

> * *

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9a-working](assets/027-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9a-working.png)

> * *

> *Find the other two numbers by subtracting 6 from the total for that language.*

> * *

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9a-solution](assets/028-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz1-q9a-solution.png)

**[1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

There are 32 students in a class.

5 do not study any languages. 15 study German (G). 18 study Spanish (S).

A student is chosen at random.   
Find the probability that the student studies Spanish but not German.
parts.solution_md:
> *Reading from the Venn diagram, 12 students study Spanish but not German.*

> *Find the probability by dividing this by the total number of students.*

$\mathrm{P} ( \text{Spanish} ) = \frac{12}{32}$

$\frac{3}{8}$** [1] **
**The unsimplified fraction is accepted.**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

There are 32 students in a class.

5 do not study any languages. 15 study German (G). 18 study Spanish (S).

A student who studies German is chosen at random. 
Find the probability that this student also studies Spanish.
parts.solution_md:
*In total, 15 students study German.* *Of these, 6 of them also study Spanish.*

> *Find the probability by dividing the number who study both by the total number of students who study German.*

$\mathrm{P} ( \text{Student} \text{who} \text{studies} \text{German} \text{also} \text{studies} \text{Spanish} ) = \frac{6}{15}$

$\frac{2}{5}$** [1]**
** The unsimplified fraction is accepted.**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Find the probability that the number is in set $A'$.
parts.solution_md:
> *A**' is the set of all numbers that **aren't** in **A**.  (It's called the 'complement' of** A.**) *
*Basically, the question is asking you 'What's the probability that the number isn't in set **A**?'*

$A ' = \{ 10 , 11 , 13 , 14 , 16 , 17 , 19 \}$

**[1] ****You can also get this mark for indicating where set A' is on the Venn diagram.**

> *There are 7 numbers in set **A'**. *
*There are a total of 10 numbers in the diagram.*

$\frac{7}{10}$**  [1]**

> *Start by labelling the circles in the diagram.*

![venn-1](assets/031-venn-1.png)

**[1]**

> *15 is the only number that's in **A** **and** **B**, so put that that in the 'overlap' (middle) part of the diagram. *
